ingredients.item: whole octopus , cleaned — or 600 g octopus, tentacles and body separated
Water to cover, 1 tbsp salt , 3 slices ginger , 2 scallion whites
Steamed rice , bean sprouts or mu sangchae for the cold crunch, sesame seeds

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Dry slices onto the hot grate in a single layer, 90 seconds undisturbed — you are searing color onto already-cooked octopus, so every second is flavor, not doneness.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: char marks on the faces and edges, the scored sheets curling open. The smell is toast over the ocean — clean and sweet.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Flip, brush the seared faces with glaze, 45–60 seconds, second brush-stroke, off the fire. Total grill time under 3 minutes — the simmer did the cooking and the glaze only needs to set.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: glossy brick-red slices, char at the edges. The eating test at the grill station: tender-chewy with a snap that yields (nakji's correct texture — firmer than squid, never rubber), sweet-heat over octopus depth.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Platter, sesame over, and the table eats it over rice with the cold crunchy banchan beside.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the bowl test: glaze-slicked nakji over rice with bean sprouts in the same bite — heat, chew, crunch. If every bite is all glaze, the slices were too small; wide pieces carry the balance.

storageNotes: Simmered octopus keeps 2 days refrigerated before grilling — the record's make-ahead is built in. Cooked, 2 days, into fried rice or noodles.
Variations: the no-simmer pounding path (see Note); baby octopus skips the slicing and runs whole on the jjukkumi record (#SF06); the glaze doubles on the squid record (#SF04).
